name: Герои, партия 5: двенадцать героев рулетки циклов V–VI без портрета (c5-48…c5-52, c5-74, c6-41…c6-46). Задание 30.09.2026: портреты для окон призыва, рулетки и «За души» вместо инициалов. Рецепт — jobs/heroes-batch-04.json (и принятые jobs/heroes-batch-03.json): стиль, запреты, три референса стиля, кадр по пояс, корпус вправо, камера чуть снизу, нижний край режет фигуру по поясу, низ без плашки; способ «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md). Редкость не рисуем, класс — по оружию или действию, школа — по цвету света. Источники: design/ui/roster.js (who, ch). Лор мест: город магов парит над проломом, внизу остались внешние ворота (главы Ведны, Ассии, Гуннара); первый зал под Эндалором — зал глиняных образцов Мастерской форм: колонны песка, бело-зелёные кристаллы, недолепленные тела — «всё сделано точно и спокойно», без уродства (style.md); Подземный лес — «лес без неба». Тварей из середины мира не рисуем — только угроза за правым краем. Детали, которых нет в главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no writing on paper, books, maps or stones, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood, no monsters in the picture. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes.

heroes.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the belt or the hips; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame, whatever the pose. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression. The lower part of the picture sinks gradually into deeper shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

jobs.subject: Subject: Odelia Twice, an elven woman of the great southern forest, a healer and battle mage of the Air school. Who she is: she healed at the outpost on the edge of the elven forest, where all trade goes, and took in everyone. One day everyone's clocks stopped for a moment and the day began again; she lived it a second time remembering the first — the same patients said the same words, the same bird landed on the same branch, and she handed the same cup without spilling a drop. Nobody else noticed, and she kept silent. Right now she holds out that same cup once more. Character: serene, secretive and quietly sorrowful — one who knows something she will never say; her lips closed, her gaze calm and deep, one brow faintly lifted. An elven woman with a fine, ageless face, long pointed ears, long silver-blond hair in a loose braid and grey-green eyes. Pose, the moment of the gift: the camera is low; she stands turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: her near hand holds out a plain clay cup toward the right, perfectly steady, not a drop spilling, and a spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school rises from it and flows toward the one beyond the right edge; her far hand is raised, palm up, and over it hovers a faint, ghostly copy of the same spiral, like an echo. Details that tell her story: (1) the cup is plain clay, full to the brim; (2) a small bird perches on a branch beside her; (3) a healer's satchel of herbs and bandages; (4) a long green-grey robe with a mantle; (5) behind her, on a shelf by the door, stands an identical empty cup. Place: the healer's house at the outpost on the edge of the elven forest at dusk: great pale trunks outside, a road with traders in soft focus. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the roots and the floor below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Arden Thousand-Eyes, an elf of the great southern forest, a Watcher of the Air school who cripples his foes and heals his friends. Who he is: the Watchers of the elven forest look through the eyes of forest creatures — usually one at a time. Once a whole flock rose over the forest edge, and he looked through all their eyes at once: the whole world from above, to the edge, to the sea and the mountains. After that, through the eyes of a single bird he saw only darkness, as if through a crack in a shutter. Right now he looses the flock at the enemy. Character: intense, otherworldly and hungry — a seer who has seen too much; his head thrown back a little, his eyes glowing white, a fierce, ecstatic look. An elf with a long, hollow-cheeked face, long pointed ears and long dark hair lifted by the wind. Pose, the moment of the flock: the camera is low; he stands at the forest edge, turned toward the right. He has exactly two arms: his near arm is flung out toward the right with the fingers spread, and a huge flock of dark birds bursts from behind him and streams toward the right in a roaring spiral, carried by white-green wind of the Air school; his far hand is pressed to his temple. Details that tell his story: (1) his eyes glow pale white — he is seeing through a thousand others; (2) a mantle of grey and black feathers; (3) a strip of cloth hangs loose around his neck — a blindfold he has pulled down; (4) a satchel of resin and healing tinctures; (5) feathers whirl around him. Place: the edge of the elven forest above a wide plain at dusk: great trees behind him, the sky full of birds. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the roots below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Orest the Thunderous, a man of the floating city of mages, a warrior-mage of the Air school. Who he is: a warrior-mage holds a weapon in one hand and a spell-gauntlet in the other, and he was one of the best — he won his duels in the circle both with steel and with air. For twenty years he believed that a blow he had not seen had not been invented yet. Then he lost a duel to a woman of his own wing and admitted it aloud — and added what the rules do not require: that no one had ever struck such a blow. Right now he strikes with both hands at once. Character: proud, honourable and fiery — a champion who can lose with dignity; his teeth bared in a battle cry, his eyes blazing. A powerful man in his forties with a short dark beard, a shaved head and a scar across his nose. Pose, the moment of the double strike: the camera is low; he lunges toward the right in the duelling circle. He has exactly two arms: his near hand thrusts forward toward the right a gauntlet set with three pale green crystals, and a thunderclap of white-green wind of the Air school bursts from it; his far hand swings a straight sword back over his shoulder, ready to follow. Details that tell his story: (1) the gauntlet is of dark steel and leather with three pale crystals across the knuckles; (2) a light duelling coat of a mage with the sleeves cut short; (3) a bruise and a split brow from the last duel; (4) a belt with a small pouch of crystals; (5) the pale stone ring of the duelling circle around him. Place: a circle of duels in a floating city of mages at dusk: a ring of pale stones, spectators blurred on the terraces, clouds and open sky beyond the edge of the city. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the stones of the circle below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Vedna Tally-Bone, an elven woman of the great southern forest, a swift archer of the Air school who cripples her foes. Who she is: when all the peoples first stood together, she went with every elf who could hold a bow to the city at the middle of the world and was set on the wall by the gate. She kept count on a long pale bone — a notch for every shot that did not need repeating. When the city rose into the sky, the wall rose with it, but the outer gate stayed on the ground, and she stayed at the gate. Her arrows ran out before the enemies did; a northerner brought her arrows carved from pale bone — they flew crooked, and she learned to shoot again. Right now she draws one of those crooked arrows. Character: steady, dry-humoured and unbreakable; her eyes narrowed, her mouth a thin determined line. An elven woman with a lean, weathered face, long pointed ears and long dark hair in a single braid with a few grey strands. Pose, the moment of the shot: the camera is low; she stands at the lonely gate, turned toward the right, the bow at full draw. She has exactly two arms: her near arm holds a long elven bow out toward the right; her far hand draws a pale, slightly crooked arrow of bone back to her cheek, and a thin spiral of pale white-green wind of the Air school straightens its flight. Details that tell her story: (1) a long pale bone hangs at her belt, covered along its length with tiny tally notches; (2) a quiver of crooked pale arrows; (3) a worn green cloak, torn and patched; (4) a scarred leather guard on her bow arm; (5) far above her, the city floating in the sky like a cloud. Place: the old outer gate standing alone on bare ground, the wall broken away, dust and a grey sky; a great city hangs in the air high above. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the ground below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Assia the Slowing, a woman of the city of mages, a battle mage of the Time school who cripples her foes. Who she is: when the city rose into the sky, she stayed below at the gate: someone had to stretch the steps of those who came at the gate, so that the others had time to meet them. The enemy walks but never arrives — that was all her magic, and in those days it asked nothing in return. Right now she stretches the enemy's step into eternity. Character: calm, ironic and quietly heroic — she laughs first; a faint smile, her eyes bright and steady. A woman in her fifties with a lined, clever face and short silver hair. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; she stands at the gate, turned toward the right. She has exactly two arms: both her hands are raised toward the right, palms open, and a wide wall of slowly turning green light of the Time school spreads in front of her; dust, pebbles and sparks hang frozen in mid-air inside it. Just beside her far hand a falling teacup hangs motionless in the air, a single drop of tea frozen above it. Details that tell her story: (1) the frozen teacup and the frozen drop — her old habit; (2) a mage's robe of the Time school, dusty and patched; (3) a small hourglass on a chain around her neck, its sand standing still; (4) laugh lines around her eyes; (5) the city floating high in the sky above the gate. Place: the lonely gate before the old road at dusk, the wall broken away, the great city hanging high overhead. Green light of the Time school rises from the ground below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Gunnar Lower-Deck, a dwarf, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: he riveted the great machine beneath the city with his crew and knew it could lift the city; nobody thought it would have to. The crew joked that the city is a ship and the ground beneath it the lower deck. When the enemy reached the gate and the key was turned, he stayed below: someone had to hold the gate while the machine lifted. They threw him a rope from above; he gave it to a wounded man. Right now he holds the gate. Character: gruff, steady and unbreakable — a dwarf who counts in shifts; his jaw clenched under his beard, his brows lowered, his eyes on the enemy, never once looking up. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a long red-brown beard braided and bound with iron rivets. Pose, the moment of holding: the camera is low; he stands in the gateway, turned toward the right, his shoulder behind his shield. He has exactly two arms: his near arm drives a great round shield of riveted iron plates forward toward the right against the blows; his far hand grips a heavy riveting hammer. Amber-orange light of the Earth school bursts from the ground under the impact. Details that tell his story: (1) the shield is studded with rivets like the machine he built; (2) a riveter's leather coat and heavy gauntlets; (3) a rope hangs down from the sky just behind him, its end lying loose on the ground; (4) his shield arm is stiff and bent — it has held too long; (5) far above, the underside of the floating city fills the sky. Place: the outer gate on bare ground at dusk, dust and a broken wall, the great city hanging overhead. Amber light rises from the cracks in the ground below.

jobs.subject: Subject: Amalia the Returned, a woman of the western harbor, a swift fighter of the Air school. Who she is: in the western harbor she climbed masts for a copper, and when a band was hired in a tavern to go down below, they called her first — there would be climbing below, they said. She stepped into the portal third. Below was a hall whose vault was lost in darkness, where sand poured in streams and stood in columns, a cold white-green light came from the stone, and unfinished bodies of clay came out of the walls — only the clay was warm. She broke one with her axe and looked inside: there was no hourglass in its chest, only dense clay. Right now she swings at a clay figure. Character: bold, quick and fearless — a sailor girl who looks inside things; a fierce grin, bright eyes. A wiry woman in her twenties, sun-browned, with short sun-bleached hair tied with a rag and a scar on her chin. Pose, the moment of the swing: the camera is low; she swings forward toward the right on a rope, her body twisting into the blow. She has exactly two arms: her near hand swings a short hand-axe down toward the right, and a white-green gust of the Air school trails the blade; her far hand grips a rope that hangs from the darkness above. Details that tell her story: (1) a sailor's striped shirt with the sleeves torn off; (2) a coil of rope over her shoulder; (3) clay dust spattered on her arms; (4) a copper coin on a cord at her neck; (5) a column of falling sand behind her. Place: a vast calm underground hall of unfinished clay figures: columns of pouring sand, white-green crystals glowing in the stone, smooth half-formed clay bodies emerging from the walls in soft focus, made precisely and calmly. White-green light rises from the crystals below; the clay glows faintly warm.

jobs.subject: Subject: Gottfried of the Forty, a man of the golden age, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: at the start of the golden age everyone who had little and wanted much went down below, and he gathered forty — debtors, younger sons, two sister-weavers, an old herbwoman. He promised them only one thing: that he would go first, wherever they went. At the exit portal he stepped in first to show it was not frightening, and woke alone on the platform above; the portal gave back no one else. Ten days later he went down again, alone, with a rope, a lamp and forty names. Right now he strides into the clay hall, calling the first name. Character: grim, loyal and unbreakable — a leader who keeps his one promise; his mouth open as he calls a name, his eyes searching the darkness, his brow furrowed. A big, broad man in his forties with a short dark beard streaked with grey and a weathered face. Pose, the moment of the descent: the camera is low; he strides toward the right through the hall. He has exactly two arms: his near arm raises a heavy round shield of oak and iron toward the right, toward a clay figure looming at the edge of the light, and amber-orange light of the Earth school runs along its rim; his far hand holds a lamp high, its warm light spilling ahead. Details that tell his story: (1) a coil of rope over his shoulder; (2) a woven belt of a weaver, tied in a particular knot, is bound around his shield arm; (3) his lips move — he calls the names one after another; (4) a dusty travelling coat over a mail shirt; (5) columns of pouring sand around him. Place: a vast calm underground hall of unfinished clay figures: columns of falling sand, white-green crystals glowing in the stone, smooth half-formed clay bodies emerging from the walls in soft focus. Amber light rises from cracks in the floor below; warm lamplight.
